summary: The account address redirects to the provider's separate sign-in service on another origin. A public write-up names the parameters that service accepts but shows no field of the page a browser receives, so nothing is filled.

sources.title: This repository's review of the Tesla preset: the redirect to the sign-in service
A third-party description of the sign-in service for non-browser clients, last changed 2023-03-14

staysInteractive.note: The write-up describes a firewall that blocks repeated requests and a protection that requires running the page's script when the client looks like a browser.
The write-up describes a passcode field for accounts with multi-factor sign-in (2023).

lookedFor: robots.txt of www.tesla.com: HTTP 403 at 19:02:36 UTC on 2026-10-12 to a plain request without a browser user agent. The body was a denial page of the site's edge server; fragments: "Access Denied", "You don't have permission to access". The rules could not be read.

The terms page of www.tesla.com (/legal/terms): the fetch tool reported HTTP 403 between 19:03 and 19:08 UTC on 2026-10-12 and returned no body; the exact time was not recorded. After these two refusals no other client and no further request was tried, and the page was not rendered.
This repository's review notes: opening the account address redirected to the provider's sign-in service at auth.tesla.com. No markup.

A third-party write-up at commit 08ad7b1, last changed 2023-03-14: the sign-in page is /oauth2/v3/authorize on auth.tesla.com; its form carries hidden session fields and is posted back with parameters named identity and credential. It describes a client that is not a browser and says a browser-like client is served a script-based protection instead. It shows no field markup.

KeePassXC-Browser's site list (commit 8b0b2c4) has no entry for this site. Chromium's public password-manager site tests (commit 88f1fe85) hold no recipes. Mozilla's published password recipes (13 records, read 2026-10-12) have no entry for this sign-in.
neededFromUser: In your own browser, signed out: open https://www.tesla.com/teslaaccount, let it send you to the sign-in service, and save the sign-in page. If the password is asked on a second page, save that one too before typing the password. Note the address of each up to the question mark. Save each as Webpage, Complete (HTML only re-downloads the address and misses a scripted or submitted form). Keep the files outside the repository: they can hold your account name. Import: node scripts/capture-login-page.mjs --id tesla --from-file <file.html>
notes: Sign-in is on another origin than the catalog address. A steps file would have to list that origin as a credential origin. It is not listed, and no steps are written from parameter names: no field of the page has been seen, and the one source says a browser is served something else.
